**Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/language_spec.rs` — LanguageSpecEngine. All checks go into `check_class_rules` (has `class: &ClassMeta`). No new modules or files in `crates/`.

## Checks & official messages (all Error)

| ID | Message |
|----|---------|
| MABSEAC | Instance properties and methods are illegal in classes that are both Sealed and Abstract. |
| MABSEAM | A method cannot be both Abstract and Sealed. |
| MCAPP | Private property cannot be Abstract. |
| MCCBS | A superclass constructor is being called, but VAR_NAME is not a declared superclass name. |
| MCCBU | This superclass constructor is called after a use of the constructed object. |
| MCCMC | Constructor for superclass can only be called once. |
| MCCSOP | Unable to modify Constant property VAR_NAME. |
| MCGSA | Method VAR_NAME tries to set or get an abstract property. |
| MCMIO | Method has too many inputs or outputs. |
| MCMSP | Private method cannot be Abstract. |
| MCMTP | TestParameterDefinition methods must be Static. |
| MCPIN | Unable to initialize class property to an instance of the class itself. |
| MCPSG | Set or get method must be fully defined in the class definition file. |
| MCSCC | To call the superclass constructor, the subclass constructor name must match the subclass name. |
| MCSCF | A superclass constructor must be assigned to the first constructor output argument. |
| MCSCM | To call a superclass method, the method name must match the subclass method name. |
| MCSCN | Method VAR_NAME tries to set a constant property. |
| MCSCO | A superclass constructor must be called using the first constructor output argument. |
| MCSCT | Superclass constructor call must not be conditionalized or be part of another expression. |
| MCSMO | Returning multiple outputs from a superclass object initialization is not supported. |
| MCSWA | A sealed class cannot specify allowed subclasses. |
| MTAGS3 | Cannot use the Access attribute when using the SetAccess or GetAccess attribute. |
| MTMAT | Attribute can only be set once. |
| MWKCL | A WeakHandle property must restrict its type using a class validation. |
| MWKCT | Specifying both WeakHandle and Constant attributes on the same property is not supported. |
| MWKREF | Specifying both WeakHandle and Dependent attributes is invalid. |

## Existing infrastructure (reuse!)

`check_class_rules` already calls: MCFIL, MCDIR, MCRED, MCCBD, setter/getter signatures, MCEB, MCANI, MCASC, MCSGA, MCSGP. New checks slot into the same function.

Key data available:
- `ClassMeta`: `name`, `superclasses`, `attributes` (Vec\<AttributeMeta\>), `properties_blocks`, `methods_blocks`, `events_blocks`, `enumeration_blocks`
- `ClassMeta` helpers: `is_sealed()`, `is_abstract()`, `is_handle()`, `has_attribute()`, `attribute_value()`
- `PropertiesBlockMeta`: `attributes` (Vec\<AttributeMeta\>), `properties` (Vec\<PropertyMeta\>)
- `MethodsBlockMeta`: `attributes` (Vec\<AttributeMeta\>), `methods` (Vec\<FunctionMeta\>)
- `FunctionMeta`: `name`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `is_constructor`, `is_setter`, `is_getter`, `is_abstract`, `method_attributes`, `byte_range`, `line`
- `PropertyMeta`: `name`, `dimensions`, `type_constraint`, `validators`, `default_value`, `has_default`
- `AttributeMeta`: `name`, `value` (Option\<String\>), `negated` (bool)
- `ctx.tree` / `ctx.source` available for tree walking when needed

## Detection (grouped by pattern)

### A. Attribute conflicts (class-level, metadata only)

**MABSEAC** — Class is both Sealed AND Abstract AND has instance members (non-abstract properties or methods in blocks without Abstract attribute).
- `class.is_sealed() && class.is_abstract()`
- Check: any `properties_block` has at least one property AND the block does NOT have `Abstract` attribute, OR any `methods_block` has at least one non-abstract method AND the block does NOT have `Abstract` attribute.
- Fire on the classdef node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef (Sealed, Abstract) Foo
      properties
          x double = 5
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire** (no instance members):
  ```matlab
  classdef (Sealed, Abstract) Foo
      properties (Abstract)
          x
      end
      methods (Abstract)
          m(obj)
      end
  end
  ```

**MCSWA** — Class is Sealed AND has `AllowedSubclasses` in its attributes.
- `class.is_sealed() && class.has_attribute("AllowedSubclasses")`
- Fire on the classdef node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef (Sealed, AllowedSubclasses = {?Bar}) Foo
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef (AllowedSubclasses = {?Bar}) Foo
  end
  ```

**MTMAT** — Same attribute name appears twice on any single attribute list (class, properties block, methods block).
- Scan `class.attributes` for duplicate names; scan each `properties_blocks[i].attributes`; scan each `methods_blocks[i].attributes`.
- Fire on the duplicate attribute's byte range.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef (Sealed, Sealed) Foo
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef (Sealed) Foo
  end
  ```

**MTAGS3** — On a properties block or methods block, `Access` appears alongside `SetAccess` or `GetAccess`.
- For each `properties_blocks[i].attributes` and `methods_blocks[i].attributes`, check if any attribute has `name == "Access"` AND any other has `name == "SetAccess"` or `name == "GetAccess"`.
- Fire on the block's attribute list.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties (Access = public, SetAccess = private)
          x double = 5
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties (SetAccess = private, GetAccess = public)
          x double = 5
      end
  end
  ```

### B. Abstract/Sealed method & property rules

**MABSEAM** — A method's `method_attributes` contains both `Abstract` and `Sealed` (non-negated).
- Iterate `methods_blocks[i].methods`; check `method_attributes` for both.
- Fire on the function_definition/function_signature node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      methods (Abstract, Sealed)
          m(obj)
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      methods (Abstract)
          m(obj)
      end
  end
  ```

**MCMSP** — A method is Abstract (`is_abstract == true`) AND its `method_attributes` contains `Access = private`.
- `func.is_abstract && func.method_attributes.iter().any(|a| a.name == "Access" && a.value.as_deref() == Some("private"))`
- Fire on the function_signature node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      methods (Abstract, Access = private)
          m(obj)
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      methods (Abstract, Access = public)
          m(obj)
      end
  end
  ```

**MCAPP** — A properties block has `Abstract` AND `Access = private` attributes.
- For each `properties_blocks[i]`, check `attributes` for both `Abstract` and `Access = private`.
- Fire on each property in the block (or once on the block node).
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties (Abstract, Access = private)
          x
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties (Abstract)
          x
      end
  end
  ```

**MCGSA** — A set/get method tries to access an abstract property. Detection: if a property is in a block with `Abstract` attribute, and there exists a `set.PropName` or `get.PropName` method.
- Build set of abstract property names from all `properties_blocks` with `Abstract` attribute.
- For each setter/getter in methods, extract prop name; if it's in the abstract set, fire.
- Fire on the set/get method node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties (Abstract)
          x
      end
      methods
          function val = get.x(obj)
              val = 0;
          end
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties
          x double = 0
      end
      methods
          function val = get.x(obj)
              val = obj.x;
          end
      end
  end
  ```

**MCPSG** — A set/get method is abstract (is a `function_signature` with no body). Interpretation: "not fully defined in the class definition file" means the setter/getter is declared as abstract (no implementation).
- Check each setter/getter: if `func.is_abstract`, fire.
- Fire on the function_signature node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties
          x
      end
      methods (Abstract)
          set.x(obj, val)
          val = get.x(obj)
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties
          x double = 0
      end
      methods
          function set.x(obj, val)
              obj.x = val;
          end
          function val = get.x(obj)
              val = obj.x;
          end
      end
  end
  ```

### C. Constant property rules (need tree walking)

These require walking method/constructor bodies to detect assignments to Constant properties.

**MCCSOP** — A constructor or method assigns to a Constant property (e.g., `obj.PropName = ...` where PropName is in a Constant block).
1. Build set of constant property names: iterate `properties_blocks`; if block has `Constant` attribute, collect all property names.
2. Find the constructor: iterate `methods_blocks[i].methods`; if `is_constructor`, get its `byte_range`.
3. Use `ctx.tree` to find the `function_definition` node matching the constructor's byte_range.
4. Walk the function body for `assignment` nodes where the LHS is a `field_expression` with `obj.Self` or `PropertyName` matching a constant.
5. Fire on the assignment node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties (Constant)
          MAX = 100
      end
      methods
          function obj = Foo()
              obj.MAX = 200;
          end
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties (Constant)
          MAX = 100
      end
      methods
          function obj = Foo()
              obj.MAX;  % just reading, not assigning
          end
      end
  end
  ```

**MCSCN** — Same as MCCSOP but for any method (not just constructor). A non-setter/getter method assigns to a Constant property.
- Same approach as MCCSOP but iterate all methods.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties (Constant)
          MAX = 100
      end
      methods
          function update(obj)
              obj.MAX = 999;
          end
      end
  end
  ```

### D. WeakHandle property rules (metadata only)

**MWKCL** — A properties block has `WeakHandle` attribute but properties in the block lack a `type_constraint`.
- For each `properties_blocks[i]` with `WeakHandle` attribute: check each property's `type_constraint`. If any property has `type_constraint == None`, fire.
- Fire on the property node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < handle
      properties (WeakHandle)
          x  % no type constraint
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < handle
      properties (WeakHandle)
          x double  % has type constraint
      end
  end
  ```

**MWKCT** — A properties block has both `WeakHandle` and `Constant` attributes.
- For each `properties_blocks[i].attributes`: check if both `WeakHandle` and `Constant` are present (non-negated).
- Fire on the block's attribute list.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < handle
      properties (WeakHandle, Constant)
          x double = 0
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < handle
      properties (WeakHandle)
          x double = 0
      end
  end
  ```

**MWKREF** — A properties block has both `WeakHandle` and `Dependent` attributes.
- Same approach as MWKCT but check for `Dependent`.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < handle
      properties (WeakHandle, Dependent)
          x
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < handle
      properties (WeakHandle)
          x double = 0
      end
  end
  ```

### E. Constructor/superclass rules (need tree walking of constructor body)

These require finding the constructor `function_definition` node via `ctx.tree`, then walking its `block` child to find `super()` or `superclass_name()` call patterns.

**Helper needed:** `find_constructor_node(class, ctx)` — Walk `ctx.tree` to find the `function_definition` whose `name` field matches `class.name`. Return the node. Then walk its `block` child to find all `function_call` nodes.

For the following checks, detect `super(args)` calls (function_call where function name is `"super"`) or `SuperclassName(args)` calls (function_call where function name matches a superclass name in `class.superclasses`).

**MCSCC** — If a method calls a superclass constructor by name, that method must be the constructor (method name == class name).
- Walk all methods; for each non-constructor method, check if its body contains a `function_call` where the called function name matches any name in `class.superclasses`. If so, fire.
- Fire on the method node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < Bar
      methods
          function doStuff(obj)
              obj = Bar(obj);  % superclass call in non-constructor
          end
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < Bar
      methods
          function obj = Foo(obj)
              obj = Bar(obj);  % superclass call in constructor
          end
      end
  end
  ```

**MCCBS** — A `super()` call references a name that is NOT in `class.superclasses`.
- In the constructor body, find `function_call` nodes where the called function name is NOT `"super"` AND does NOT match any name in `class.superclasses`. If it looks like a constructor call (assignment pattern `obj = Name(obj)`), fire.
- Fire on the function_call node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < Bar
      methods
          function obj = Foo(obj)
              obj = Baz(obj);  % Baz is not a superclass
          end
      end
  end
  ```

**MCCBU** — A superclass constructor is called after the constructed object has been used (assigned to, passed to a function, etc.).
- In the constructor body, track statement order. If the `super()` or `Superclass(obj)` call appears after any use of the first output variable, fire.
- Fire on the super call node.

**MCCMC** — The superclass constructor is called more than once in the constructor body.
- Count `super()` or `Superclass(obj)` calls in the constructor body. If count > 1, fire on the second occurrence.

**MCSCF** — The superclass constructor call must be assigned to the first constructor output argument.
- Find the super call; check that it's in an `assignment` node and the LHS is the first output variable name.
- Fire on the assignment if LHS != first output.

**MCSCO** — The superclass constructor must use the first constructor output argument as input.
- Find the super call; check that the first argument is the first output variable.
- Fire on the function_call if first arg != first output.

**MCSCT** — The super call must not be inside an `if_statement`, `switch_statement`, `try_statement`, or nested inside another expression.
- Check the parent chain of the super call node. If any ancestor (up to the constructor's block) is `if_statement`, `switch_statement`, `try_statement`, fire.

**MCSMO** — The super call outputs are destructured into multiple variables.
- If the assignment LHS is a `multioutput_variable` (e.g., `[obj, x] = super(args)`), fire.

**MCSCM** — A non-constructor method calls a superclass method using `super.MethodName()` where the method name doesn't match the subclass method name.
- In each non-constructor method, find `method_call` nodes (field_expression on super). If the method name doesn't match the enclosing method name, fire.

### F. Method signature rules

**MCMIO** — A method has more than 64 inputs or more than 64 outputs.
- For each method in `methods_blocks[i].methods`: if `func.inputs.len() > 64` or `func.outputs.len() > 64` (excluding `~`), fire.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      methods
          function [a1,a2,...,a65] = manyOutputs(obj)  % >64 outputs
          end
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      methods
          function [a,b,c] = fewOutputs(obj)
          end
      end
  end
  ```

**MCMTP** — A method named `TestParameterDefinition` is not in a `Static` methods block.
- For each method: if `func.name == "TestParameterDefinition"` AND `func.method_attributes` does NOT contain `Static` (non-negated), fire.
- Fire on the method node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < matlab.unittest.TestCase
      methods
          function p = TestParameterDefinition()
              p = {1, 2, 3};
          end
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo < matlab.unittest.TestCase
      methods (Static)
          function p = TestParameterDefinition()
              p = {1, 2, 3};
          end
      end
  end
  ```

**MCPIN** — A property is initialized to an instance of the class itself. Detection: check each property's `default_value` — if it contains a call to the class name (e.g., `Foo()` in class `Foo`).
- For each property with `has_default == true`: check `default_value` text for a `function_call` pattern matching `ClassName()`.
- Use `ctx.tree` to find the property node and check its `default_value` child for a function_call with the class name.
- Fire on the property node.
- **MUST fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties
          x Foo = Foo()  % initialized to instance of itself
      end
  end
  ```
- **MUST NOT fire:**
  ```matlab
  classdef Foo
      properties
          x double = 0
      end
  end
  ```

## Implementation approach

1. Add all 26 check calls inside `check_class_rules` after the existing calls.
2. Group A–D checks: pure metadata inspection of `ClassMeta`, `PropertiesBlockMeta`, `MethodsBlockMeta`, `FunctionMeta`, `PropertyMeta`.
3. Group E checks: require a helper to find the constructor `function_definition` node via `ctx.tree` (match by name against `class.name`), then DFS-walk its `block` child. Collect all `function_call` nodes that look like superclass calls. Apply checks against this collected set.
4. Group F checks: metadata inspection, except MCPIN which may need tree walking to inspect property default_value children.
5. Update the `//!` module doc table in `language_spec.rs` to list all 26 new check IDs.

## Files

- `crates/mlt_rules/src/language_spec.rs` — extend `check_class_rules`, add sub-check methods, module doc rows, tests. No new modules.
- `docs/<id>.md` per check (26 pages) — follow `docs/nosemi.md` template:
  - Title: `# <ID> - <Human Name>`
  - Default severity + category + can-be-disabled
  - "What this rule does" / "Why this matters"
  - Examples: Correct / Incorrect / Fixed (MATLAB code blocks)
  - Configuration section (no params for these — just severity)
  - Target node types section
  - Related rules section
- `docs/rules.md` — add 26 rows to the rule table.
- `zensical.toml` — add 26 nav entries under `Rules` section.

## Tests

For each of the 26 checks, add two tests in `language_spec.rs::tests`:
1. `test_<id>_fires` — MATLAB code that triggers the check; assert `filter_by_id(&diags, "<ID>")` is non-empty.
2. `test_<id>_no_fire` — valid MATLAB code; assert `filter_by_id(&diags, "<ID>")` is empty.

Plus one test for config-disabled behavior (already handled by the engine being off).

Total: ~52 tests (26 × 2). Group E tests need complete classdef fixtures with constructor bodies.

## Key pitfalls

- **FunctionMeta doesn't store the tree-sitter node.** For Group E (and MCPIN, MCCSOP, MCSCN), use `ctx.tree` to find the relevant `function_definition` or `property` node by matching `byte_range` from FunctionMeta/PropertyMeta.
- **`function_call` doubles as indexing.** For superclass call detection, look for `function_call` nodes where the function name matches a superclass or is `"super"`, AND the node is in an assignment context (LHS is the constructor output).
- **Attribute negation.** Use `!a.negated` when checking for attribute presence (e.g., `Sealed` but not `~Sealed`).
- **Per-property attributes don't exist.** MATLAB properties block attributes (WeakHandle, Constant, Dependent, Abstract, Access) are block-level, not per-property. All properties in a block share attributes.
- **MCMIO limit is 64.** MATLAB allows up to 64 inputs and 64 outputs per function (excluding `~`).
- **Many classdef test fixtures need `end` keywords.** Tree-sitter-matlab requires `end` for classdef, methods, properties blocks in some configurations. Always include `end` in test fixtures.

| FVOOD | Specifying a default value for an output argument is not supported. |
| FVOOI | Use of ignored arguments in output arguments block is not supported. |
| FVOON | Using name-value argument as output argument is not supported. |
| FVORDI | Ignored input arguments are not allowed after a Repeating arguments block or name-value arguments. |
| FVORDN | Positional arguments must be defined before name-value arguments. |
| FVORDO | Repeating output arguments must be defined after required output arguments. |
| FVORDP | Positional arguments must be defined in the following order: required, optional, and repeating. |

| FVREPD | Default values are not supported in a Repeating arguments block. |
| FVREPO | Repeating input arguments block containing varargin must not have other arguments. |
| FVSOR | Input arguments block declarations and the function line must contain the same input arguments in the same order. |
| FVSORO | Output arguments block declarations and the function line must contain the same output arguments. |
| FVUBD | Argument is referenced before it is declared in the arguments block. |
| FVVCON | For input arguments, validation functions must only use previously declared positional arguments, the argument being validated, or literals. |
| FVVIN | Validation function must use the argument as an input. |
| FVVREP | varargin can only be used inside repeating input arguments block. |
| TINVALDIM | Each dimension must be a nonnegative integer number or a colon. |
| TTOOFEWDIMS | Specify at least two dimensions for size. |

## Existing infrastructure (reuse!)
`check_function_validation(meta, ctx, diagnostics)` currently calls `check_fvnst` + `check_vtpod` (vtpod is a no-op stub — implemented in syntax_errors from Wave B, leave the stub). `FunctionMeta` provides: name, inputs, outputs, is_constructor, is_setter, is_getter, has_arguments_block, argument_validations (Vec<ArgValidation> with name/dimensions/type_constraint/validators/default_value), byte_range, line, end_line, is_method, is_abstract, method_attributes.

**CRITICAL LIMITATION:** `FunctionMeta.argument_validations` is a FLAT `Vec<ArgValidation>` that loses block grouping. It does NOT tell you:
- Which `arguments_statement` block a validation belongs to
- The block's attributes (Input/Output/Repeating)
- The ordering of blocks

Therefore: **All block-level structural checks must work with raw `arguments_statement` AST nodes directly.** `ArgValidation` is only useful for simple per-property checks (e.g., TINVALDIM, TTOOFEWDIMS) where block context doesn't matter.

## Required new data structures

### `ArgumentsBlockMeta` (new struct in `language_spec.rs` or `metadata.rs`)

```rust
/// A single arguments block with its attributes and parsed properties.
struct ArgumentsBlockMeta {
    /// The raw tree-sitter node for this arguments_statement.
    node: tree_sitter::Node,
    /// Attributes on this block: (Input), (Output), (Repeating), etc.
    attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
    /// Parsed argument validations in declaration order.
    args: Vec<ArgValidation>,
    /// Byte range of the block.
    byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
}
```

### Helper function to extract grouped blocks

```rust
/// Extract all arguments blocks from a function, grouped with attributes.
fn extract_arguments_blocks_grouped(
    func_node: tree_sitter::Node,
    source: &str,
) -> Vec<ArgumentsBlockMeta>
```

This walks `func_node.children()`, finds each `arguments_statement`, extracts its `attributes` child (using `extract_attributes` from metadata.rs), and extracts `property` children into `Vec<ArgValidation>`.

### Helper to detect name-value syntax

A `Name=value` argument in the AST is a `property` node whose first child is NOT just an `identifier` but instead has a structure like `property_name = expression`. Specifically, check if the property node has a child of kind `"default_value"` or if the name is followed by `=`. Alternatively, detect by checking if `ArgValidation.name` contains `=` or if the raw AST property node has a `=` child after the name.

### Helper to classify block role

```rust
fn block_role(block: &ArgumentsBlockMeta) -> BlockRole {
    // Check attributes for "Input", "Output", "Repeating"
    // Default (no attributes) = implicit Input
}
```

## Detection (grouped by pattern)

### A. Arguments-block structure (per function, via raw AST + ArgumentsBlockMeta)
- Multiple Repeating blocks → FVDREP
- Both 'Input' and 'Output' attributes on same block → FVIOA
- Repeating input block with varargin + other args → FVREPO
- varargin outside repeating input block → FVVREP
- varargout outside repeating output block → FVOVREP
- Repeating blocks with name-value args → FVNREP
- Repeating blocks with default values → FVREPD
- Multiple repeating output args → FORM
- Default value for output arg → FVOOD
- Ignored args in output block → FVOOI
- Name-value arg as output → FVOON
- Ignored input args after Repeating/name-value → FVORDI
- Positional before name-value order → FVORDN
- Positional order required/optional/repeating → FVORDP
- Repeating output after required output → FVORDO
- Input blocks before output blocks → FVOBI
- Validation/default on ignored args → FVIDV
- Attribute values must be logical constants → FVATF
- Banned functions in arguments blocks → FVBTN (eval, evalin, evalc, feval, etc.)
- Nested function calls in arguments blocks → FVNSC
- Name-value with class name + default → FVNDE
- Name-value with class name + validation → FVNVL
- Multiple name-value structs with class name → FVMCL
- Name-value in default values → FVOND
- Name-value without dotted name in validation → FVONV
- Arg referenced before declared → FVUBD
- Same name as name-value struct and positional → FVDAN
- Positional declared once → FVDAP
- Name-value declared once → FVDNF

### B. Order/consistency with function line (via FunctionMeta.inputs/outputs + raw AST)
- Input args block order != function line order → FVSOR
- Output args block order != function line order → FVSORO
- Arg in arguments block not an input to function → FVNIV

### C. Validation function rules (via ArgValidation.validators + raw AST)
- Validation functions must use the argument as input → FVVIN
- Input validation functions only use previously declared positional args / the arg / literals → FVVCON
- Output validation functions only use the arg / literals → FVOCON
- Dimensions must be nonnegative integer or colon → TINVALDIM
- At least two dimensions → TTOOFEWDIMS
- name=value args must be at the end → FVAPN

## Implementation approach

### Step 1: Add helper infrastructure to `language_spec.rs`

Add `ArgumentsBlockMeta` struct and `extract_arguments_blocks_grouped()` helper. Add helper functions:
- `block_role(block) -> BlockRole` (Input/Output/Repeating/Default)
- `is_name_value_arg(arg_node, source) -> bool`
- `get_block_arg_names(block, source) -> Vec<String>` (extracts property names from raw AST)

### Step 2: Extend `check_function_validation` to iterate all functions

```rust
fn check_function_validation(&self, meta: &FileMeta, ctx: &FileContext, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
    self.check_fvnst(ctx, diagnostics);  // existing
    self.check_vtpod(meta, diagnostics); // existing no-op stub
    
    // For each function that has arguments blocks:
    for func in meta.functions.iter().chain(meta.local_functions.iter()) {
        if !func.has_arguments_block { continue; }
        let blocks = extract_arguments_blocks_grouped(/* func AST node */, ctx.source);
        self.check_arguments_structure(func, &blocks, ctx, diagnostics);
        self.check_arguments_ordering(func, &blocks, diagnostics);
        self.check_validation_rules(func, &blocks, ctx, diagnostics);
    }
}
```

**Note:** To get the raw `function_definition` node for each `FunctionMeta`, we need to either:
- (a) Store the tree-sitter `Node` in `FunctionMeta` (requires metadata.rs change), OR
- (b) Re-walk the tree to find each function by byte_range, OR
- (c) Pass the tree to `check_function_validation` and re-walk to find function nodes

Option (c) is cleanest: `check_function_validation` already has `ctx` with `ctx.tree`. Walk `ctx.tree.root_node()` to find all `function_definition` nodes, match them to `meta.functions` by byte_range, then extract grouped blocks.

### Step 3: Implement checks grouped by helper function

**Group A — Structure checks** (need `ArgumentsBlockMeta`):
- `check_arguments_structure(func, blocks, ctx, diags)` handles: FVDREP, FVIOA, FVREPO, FVVREP, FVOVREP, FVNREP, FVREPD, FVOOD, FVOOI, FVOON, FVORDI, FVORDN, FVORDP, FVORDO, FVOBI, FVIDV, FVATF, FVBTN, FVNSC, FVNDE, FVNVL, FVMCL, FVOND, FVONV, FVUBD, FVDAN, FVDAP, FVDNF

**Group B — Ordering/consistency** (need `FunctionMeta.inputs/outputs` + block arg names):
- `check_arguments_ordering(func, blocks, diags)` handles: FVSOR, FVSORO, FVNIV

**Group C — Validation rules** (need `ArgValidation.validators` + raw AST):
- `check_validation_rules(func, blocks, ctx, diags)` handles: FVVIN, FVVCON, FVOCON, TINVALDIM, TTOOFEWDIMS, FVAPN

### Step 4: Add module doc rows

Add to the FV* checks table in the module doc comment at the top of `language_spec.rs`.

### Step 5: Tests

For each check, add at minimum:
- `test_<id>_fires` — MATLAB source that triggers the check
- `test_<id>_no_fire` — MATLAB source that should NOT trigger

Group tests by check ID. Example:

```rust

fn test_fvdrep_multiple_repeating_blocks() {
    let source = "\
function y = f(x)
    arguments (Repeating)
        x double
    end
    arguments (Repeating)
        y double
    end
    y = x;
end
";
    let diags = check_source(source, "f.m");
    assert!(!filter_by_id(&diags, "FVDREP").is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn test_fvdrep_no_fire_single_repeating() {
    let source = "\
function y = f(x)
    arguments (Repeating)
        x double
    end
    y = x;
end
";
    let diags = check_source(source, "f.m");
    assert!(filter_by_id(&diags, "FVDREP").is_empty());
}
```

Also add a config-disabled test:
```rust
#[test]

    // Verify all FV* checks can be disabled via config
}
```

## MUST fire
```matlab

function y = f(x)
    arguments (Repeating)
        x double
    end
    arguments (Repeating)
        y double
    end
    y = x;
end

% FVIOA: Both Input and Output on same block
function y = f(x)
    arguments (Input, Output)
        x double
        y double
    end
    y = x;
end

% FVOBI: Output block before Input block
function y = f(x)
    arguments (Output)
        y double
    end
    arguments (Input)
        x double
    end
    y = x;
end
```
(plus specific invalid-arguments-block cases per check — see tests section)

## MUST NOT fire
```matlab
function y = f(x)
    arguments
        x (1,1) double {mustBeReal}
    end
    y = x;
end
```

## Files
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/language_spec.rs` — extend `check_function_validation`, add `ArgumentsBlockMeta` struct, helper functions, sub-check methods, module doc rows, tests.
- `docs/<id>.md` per check (38 pages) — follow `docs/nosemi.md` template.
- `docs/rules.md` — 38 rows.
- `zensical.toml` — 38 nav entries in `Rules` section.

## Tests
fires/not-fires per check; config disabled. See Step 5 above for pattern.

## Pitfalls
- The `arguments_statement` AST has `attributes` child containing `attribute` nodes. Each `attribute` has an `identifier` child: `"Input"`, `"Output"`, or `"Repeating"`. Use `extract_attributes()` from metadata.rs.
- `FunctionMeta.argument_validations` is FLAT — do NOT use it for block-level checks. Use raw AST or the new `ArgumentsBlockMeta`.
- The (Input)/(Output) attribute is an `attributes` child of `arguments_statement`. To distinguish: check the identifier text inside each `attribute` child.
- `function_call` doubles as indexing in tree-sitter-matlab — irrelevant here since we're looking at arguments blocks, not function calls.
- Many checks need the raw `arguments_statement` nodes, not just parsed metadata — walk the tree per function.
- FVSOR/FVSORO need comparing arguments-block declarations with `function_arguments` / `function_output` on the function line. Use `FunctionMeta.inputs`/`FunctionMeta.outputs` for the function line, and extract property names from each block's raw AST.
- Leave the vtpod stub as-is (implemented in syntax_errors) — do not double-implement.
- `is_check_enabled` gating: all checks should be individually gateable. Use a match/if-else on check ID.
- Name-value detection: a property node has `Name=value` syntax if its children include a `=` token after the name identifier. Check raw AST, not ArgValidation.

- Fire: NCHKOS
- These functions validate nargin/nargout and do NOT return a value
- Example: `x = narginchk(a, b)` → NCHKOS
- MUST NOT fire: `narginchk(a, b);` (standalone, no assignment)

### E. Variable definition (USESWNS)

**Where:** Add to `check_script_rules` (script-level only, using SymbolTable).

**USESWNS** — Variable used before explicit definition:
- Match: In script scope, a variable use appears before any assignment to that variable
- Detection: Use the existing `SymbolTable` (already built in `check_file`). Check `scope.uses` vs `scope.defs` for ordering.
- Fire: USESWNS at the point of first use

**Overlap with SUSENS:** The `UnsetVariablesEngine` already fires `SUSENS` for the same scenario. **Resolution:** USESWNS fires with Error severity (LanguageSpecification category), SUSENS fires with Warning severity (UnsetVariables category). To avoid double-firing, add a flag in the diagnostic or check if the UnsetVariablesEngine is active. **Simpler approach:** If the UnsetVariablesEngine would fire SUSENS for the same variable, skip USESWNS. This requires either: (a) a post-pass coordination, or (b) accepting that both may fire (user can disable one via config).

**Recommended:** Implement USESWNS as a simple script-level check. Document that it may overlap with SUSENS from the UnsetVariables engine. Users can disable one via config.

## MUST fire

```matlab
spmd
    load('data.mat');          % SPLD
    save('out.mat');           % SPSV
    who;                       % SPWHOS
    evalin('caller', 'x');    % SPEVC
end
error('MyID:ERR');             % ERTXT (note: colon in ID)
warning('MyID:WRN');           % WTXT (note: colon in ID)
```

## MUST NOT fire

```matlab
spmd
    d = load('data.mat');      % assigned → no SPLD
    save('out.mat', '-fromstruct', s);   % has -fromstruct → no SPSV
    who('-file', 'data.mat');  % has -file → no SPWHOS
end
error('MyID:ERR', 'message here'); % has message → no ERTXT
error('just a message');            % no colon = message, not ID → no ERTXT
```

## Files to modify

- `crates/mlt_rules/src/language_spec.rs` — extend `check_dfs`, add `check_spmd_transparency`, `check_error_warning_rules`, `check_nchkos`, `check_ctoro`, `check_ctoine`, `check_mherit`, `check_useswns`. Update module doc comment table. Add tests.
- `docs/rules.md` — 16 rows (one per check ID)
- `zensical.toml` — 16 nav entries

**Documentation pages:** The existing sub-checks (SPNST, SPRET, etc.) do NOT have individual doc pages. Follow the existing convention: document all 16 checks in `docs/rules.md` row entries and in the module-level doc comment. Do NOT create 16 individual `docs/<id>.md` pages unless the project convention changes. (If individual pages are desired, create them for ALL existing sub-checks too, not just these 16.)

## Tests

For each check, write at least 2 tests:
1. **fires** — code that triggers the check
2. **does not fire** — equivalent code that should NOT trigger

Additional test categories:
- **Config disabled** — verify checks respect engine-level disable (if applicable)
- **Edge cases** — nested spmd, function_call vs indexing disambiguation, error with format args

Example test structure:
```rust
#[test]
fn test_ertxt_fire() {
    let source = "error('MyTool:badInput');\n";
    let diags = check_source(source, "test.m");
    let ertxt = filter_by_id(&diags, "ERTXT");
    assert!(!ertxt.is_empty(), "ERTXT should fire for error with ID but no message");
}

#[test]
fn test_ertxt_no_fire_message() {
    let source = "error('just a message');\n";
    let diags = check_source(source, "test.m");
    let ertxt = filter_by_id(&diags, "ERTXT");
    assert!(ertxt.is_empty(), "ERTXT should NOT fire for error with plain message");
}

#[test]
fn test_ertxt_no_fire_with_message() {
    let source = "error('MyTool:badInput', 'msg here');\n";
    let diags = check_source(source, "test.m");
    let ertxt = filter_by_id(&diags, "ERTXT");
    assert!(ertxt.is_empty(), "ERTXT should NOT fire when message is provided");
}
```

## Pitfalls (confirmed)

- **ERTXT/WTXT:** The colon is the key discriminator. Fire when single arg HAS a colon (ID without message). Don't fire when no colon (plain message). This is the OPPOSITE of what the original plan stated.
- **function_call ambiguity:** `function_call` in tree-sitter-matlab covers both calls and indexing. For SPMD checks, match by function name (known builtins are never array names in practice).
- **SPBRK vs SPRET:** SPRET already catches all break/continue inside spmd. SPBRK is subsumed. Defer SPBRK.
- **USESWNS vs SUSENS:** Overlap exists. Document it. Users can disable one via config.
- **SPDEC/SPDEC3:** MUST probe AST before coding. Expected: `spmd_statement` has children for bounds after the `spmd` keyword. Verify with astprobe.
- **MHERIT:** Use conservative denylist. Verify with MATLAB which builtins are truly non-subclassable.
- **NCHKOS:** Check that the function_call is on the RHS of an assignment. `narginchk(a,b);` alone is fine; `x = narginchk(a,b)` is not.
- **CTORO:** Check `function_definition` outputs. If the function name matches the class name and outputs are empty, fire.

**Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — GoodPracticesEngine. All checks gated by `is_check_enabled`, sub-checks of the engine.

## Checks & messages (all Warning unless noted)
| ID | Message |
|----|---------|
| ADPROP | Use app.VAR_NAME to refer to this property. |
| ADPROPLC | Use app.VAR_NAME to reference a property of app. |

| MCHDP | A property default value that is a handle will cause all instances to share the same object data. |
| MCHDT | Declaring the value of a property as a handle might cause all instances to share the same default handle. |
| MCNPN | VAR_NAME is referenced but is not a property, method, or event name defined in this class. |

| MHERM | Parenthesize the multiplication of VAR_NAME and its transpose to ensure the result is Hermitian. |
| MIPC1 | Calling the computer function with 'arch' returns 'win64', 'glnxa64', or 'maci64'. |
| MNUML | To create a square matrix, use VAR_NAME(numel(...), numel(...)). |
| MOBSRV | Using SetObservable or GetObservable on a Constant property has no effect. |
| MTHANS | Using ANS as a method name is not recommended. |

## Existing infrastructure
The engine already implements OOP checks (CPROP, NOIN, PROP, MEXCEP, DISPLAY). The `analysis/metadata.rs` FileMeta/ClassMeta/PropertyMeta/FunctionMeta provide class structure. Engine is node-level (check() per node) — some new checks need tree walks.

## Detection (grouped)

### A. Class/property metadata checks (file-level tree walk or metadata)
- ATTF/ATTOF: class attribute Abstract set to false or non-literal → walk class_definition attributes. Use FileMeta.class if available, else tree walk.
- MCPO: property with no effect in value class (e.g., SetAccess/GetAccess on value class properties) → metadata.
- MCSAC: SetAccess on Constant properties → metadata.
- MOBSRV: SetObservable/GetObservable on Constant property → metadata.
- MDEPIN: default value on Dependent property → metadata.
- MGMD: dependent property without get method and without private GetAccess → metadata + methods walk.
- MCHDP/MCHDT: property default value is a handle (constructor of handle class) → property default_value contains handle class constructor.
- MCCPI: Constant property without initialization and not abstract → metadata.
- MCCSPS: Constant property never modified → metadata + usage scan.
- MCNPN: reference to name not in class → symbol analysis.
- MCNPR: assignment target not a property → symbol analysis.
- MCVM/MCSNOV/MCSOH/MCSUP: set/get method return-value rules → method metadata + body scan.

### B. Node-level (function_call/assignment/range dispatch)
- ADPROP/ADPROPLC: `app.PropertyName` field access in App Designer context → field_expression where base is `app`.
- MTHANS: method named `ans` → function_definition name check.
- MHERM: `x*x'` or `x'*x` without parens → binary_operator * with transpose operand.
- M3COL: range `a:b:c:d` → range node with 3 colons (4 parts).
- CTOINW: constructed object as constructor input → function_call to class name with arg that is also a call to same class.
- MIPC1: `computer('arch')` call.
- MNUML: `zeros(numel(x))` style → function_call zeros with 1 arg where arg is numel(...).
- MCCPE: calling a property as function → function_call whose name is a property name.

## MUST fire
```matlab
classdef (Abstract = false) Foo   % ATTOF
end
x = computer('arch');             % MIPC1
y = a:b:c:d;                      % M3COL
```

## MUST NOT fire
```matlab
classdef Foo
end
x = computer;                     % MIPC1 not fired (no 'arch')
```

## Files
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — add sub-check methods + dispatch, module doc rows, tests.
- `docs/good-practices.md` engine page (if not present) or per-check rows in docs/rules.md.
- `docs/rules.md` — rows. `zensical.toml` — nav entries.

## Tests
fires/not-fires per check; config disabled.

## Pitfalls
- Metadata API: read analysis/metadata.rs for ClassMeta/PropertyMeta/FunctionMeta exact fields before coding.
- Some checks need symbol-table/tree-walk that the node-level engine can't reach from check() — the engine may need has_file_check=true (hybrid) like readability MFAMB, or tree walking via ctx.tree. Verify the engine's current architecture first.
- Confirm with astprobe before coding each pattern.

**Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — GoodPracticesEngine. All checks gated by `is_check_enabled`.

## Checks & messages (all Warning)
| ID | Message |
|----|---------|
| PFEVB | Using EVALIN('base') or ASSIGNIN('base') inside a PARFOR loop refers to the worker machines' base workspaces. |
| PFGP | Avoid assigning to GLOBAL or PERSISTENT variable VAR_NAME inside a PARFOR loop. |
| PFGV | Avoid using GLOBAL variable VAR_NAME in a PARFOR loop. |
| PFIIN | The input variable VAR_NAME should be initialized before the PARFOR loop. |
| PFOUS | The output variable VAR_NAME might not be used after the PARFOR loop. |
| PFRIN | The reduction variable VAR_NAME might not be set before the PARFOR loop. |
| PFRNI | Do not specify the increment explicitly. The parfor loop can only use an increment of one. |
| PFRUS | The reduction variable VAR_NAME might not be used after the PARFOR loop. |
| PFTUSW | The temporary variable VAR_NAME might be used after the PARFOR loop on line VAR_NUMBER. |
| PFUIXW | The index variable VAR_NAME might be used after the PARFOR loop on line VAR_NUMBER. |
| SPEVB | Using EVALIN('base') or ASSIGNIN('base') inside an SPMD block refers to the worker machines' base workspaces. |
| SPGV | Using the GLOBAL or PERSISTENT variable VAR_NAME in an SPMD block might fail because it is accessed on a worker machine. |
| DSPMDA | Distributed array must be created outside of an SPMD block. |

## Detection
These are context-aware checks requiring loop/parfor/spmd detection. The engine likely needs tree walking (parfor = for_statement with parfor keyword; spmd = spmd_statement).

### Node-level / context patterns
- PFRNI: parfor range with explicit increment (`parfor i = 1:2:10`) → for_statement range with step != 1.
- PFEVB/SPEVB: `evalin('base',...)` / `assignin('base',...)` inside parfor/spmd body.
- PFGP/PFGV/SPGV: global/persistent var assignment/use inside parfor/spmd body.
- DSPMDA: distributed array creation (gpuArray/distributed/zeros on worker) inside spmd.

### Dataflow checks (symbol table / file-level)
- PFIIN: input variable not initialized before parfor → symbol table usage analysis.
- PFOUS: output variable not used after parfor.
- PFRIN: reduction variable not set before parfor.
- PFRUS: reduction variable not used after parfor.
- PFTUSW: temporary variable used after parfor.
- PFUIXW: index variable used after parfor.

These 6 dataflow checks may be best-effort using the symbol table (`SymbolTable::build`), similar to how other engines classify loop variables.

## MUST fire
```matlab
parfor i = 1:2:10     % PFRNI
    evalin('base', 'x');  % PFEVB
    x(i) = i;
end
```

## MUST NOT fire
```matlab
parfor i = 1:10
    x(i) = i;
end
```

## Files
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — add sub-check methods + dispatch, module doc rows, tests.
- `docs/rules.md` — rows. `zensical.toml` — nav entries.

## Tests
fires/not-fires per check; config disabled.

## Pitfalls
- The good_practices engine is node-level; the parfor/spmd context + dataflow checks may require making it hybrid (has_file_check) or adding tree-walk helpers. Check the engine's current architecture first.
- Confirm with astprobe: parfor → for_statement with `parfor` keyword child; spmd → spmd_statement (verified in earlier waves).
- The 6 dataflow checks (PFIIN/PFOUS/PFRIN/PFRUS/PFTUSW/PFUIXW) are best-effort; if a specific check proves too unreliable, implement a conservative version and document the limitation.

# GOODPRAC G3 — Logical/Branch/Scalar Rules (8 checks) — Plan

**Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — GoodPracticesEngine. All checks gated by `is_check_enabled`.

## Checks & messages (all Warning)
| ID | Message |
|----|---------|
| BDLGI | Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator. |
| BDLOG1 | A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar. |
| BDLOG2 | A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar, or compare the scalar value to 0. |
| BDSCA | Unexpected use of VAR_OPERATOR in a scalar context. |
| BDSCI | Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator. |
| COMPNOP | This logical comparison simplifies to VAR_NAME(...). Did you mean to use VAR_NAME to evaluate function argument: VAR_NAME(...VAR_NAME...)? |
| COMPNOT | This logical comparison simplifies to ~VAR_NAME(...). Did you mean to use VAR_NAME to evaluate function argument: VAR_NAME(...VAR_NAME...)? |
| M3COL | Using three colons (a:b:c:d) in an expression is probably unintended. |

## Detection

### Node-level patterns (existing engine dispatch — boolean_operator, comparison_operator, if_statement, range)
- **BDLOG1/BDLOG2**: `if x` where x is an array (non-scalar) expression → in `if_statement`/`while_statement` condition, if the condition is not a comparison/boolean/scalar, fire BDLOG1. BDLOG2 variant when comparing scalar to 0. Both relate to conditional on array.
- **BDLGI**: variable assigned via nonlogical operator but used as logical → assignment where RHS is `&`, `|`, `~` result, or a var set by nonlogical op used in condition. Conservative: detect `if (var = expr)` where expr uses nonlogical ops.
- **BDSCA**: operator used on a scalar where element-wise was intended (`&`/`|` on scalars → should be `&&`/`||`; conversely `&&`/`||` on arrays). Detect `&`/`|` with scalar operands (BDSCA) and `&&`/`||` with array operands (BDSCI).
- **BDSCI**: variable set by nonscalar operator.
- **COMPNOP/COMPNOT**: logical comparison that simplifies to a function call, e.g. `x > 0` vs `logical(x)`... Actually: `if (isa(x,'double') == true)` simplifies to `isa(x,'double')`. Detect comparison `== true` / `~= false` on a function_call → COMPNOP; `== false`/`~= true` → COMPNOT.
- **M3COL**: range with 3 colons `a:b:c:d` → range node with 4 parts (3 colons). (Also in G1; implement once — assign to G3 here.)

## MUST fire
```matlab
if x > 0 && y   % BDLOG/BDSCA patterns
    z = 1;
end
a = 1:2:3:4;    % M3COL
if isa(x,'double') == true   % COMPNOP
end
```

## MUST NOT fire
```matlab
if x > 0 && y > 1
    z = 1;
end
a = 1:2:10;     % two colons, fine
```

## Files
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — add sub-check methods + dispatch, module doc rows, tests.
- `docs/rules.md` — rows. `zensical.toml` — nav entries.

## Tests
fires/not-fires per check; config disabled.

## Pitfalls
- The `&&`/`||` vs `&`/`|` distinction is the classic BDSCA/BDSCI territory — careful with operand scalar-ness. Use conservative heuristics.
- M3COL implement here (assign to G3); remove from G1 plan if duplicated.
- Confirm AST shapes (boolean_operator for `&`/`&&`, comparison_operator, range) with astprobe.

# GOODPRAC G4 — Function-Call Conventions (10 checks) — Plan

**Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — GoodPracticesEngine. All checks gated by `is_check_enabled`.

## Checks & messages (all Warning)
| ID | Message |
|----|---------|
| GTARG | Function might be called with too many arguments. |
| LTARG | Function might be called with too few arguments. |
| VTFIN | VAR_NAME should be the first input argument to the VAR_NAME function. |
| CTPCT | The format might not agree with the argument count. |
| FXSET | Loop index VAR_NAME is changed inside of a FOR loop. |
| FXUP | Outer loop index VAR_NAME is set inside a nested function. |
| SIMPT | This import statement runs before any other code in function VAR_NAME. Consider placing it at the top of the function body. |
| TLEV | VAR_NAME could be very inefficient unless it is a top-level statement in its function. |
| UNONC | Assign the onCleanup output argument to a variable. Do not use the tilde operator (~) in place of a variable. |
| MIPC1 | Calling the computer function with 'arch' returns 'win64', 'glnxa64', or 'maci64'. |

## Detection

### Node-level (function_call / for_statement / assignment dispatch)
- **GTARG/LTARG**: function called with more/fewer args than its nargin. Requires knowing the callee's arity. Conservative: fire GTARG when a known function is called with an implausible arg count, or when calling a user function whose signature (from FileMeta) has fewer params. Best-effort — may be skipped if no reliable arity source; document.
- **VTFIN**: `inputname`/`validateattributes` style — a variable should be the first arg (e.g. `fprintf`/`validateattributes` where first arg isn't the array). Detect known functions where first arg is a format/literal.
- **CTPCT**: `sprintf`/`fprintf` format string placeholder count != argument count.
- **FXSET**: loop index assigned inside its own for loop → for_statement: if iterator var appears as assignment LHS in body.
- **FXUP**: outer loop index set inside a nested function.
- **SIMPT**: `import` statement after other code in a function → block: import not first statement.
- **TLEV**: known inefficient functions (`disp`/`fprintf`/etc.) used as sub-expression not top-level statement → function_call whose parent is not statement-level.
- **UNONC**: `onCleanup(...)` used as statement without assignment, or `[~] = onCleanup(...)` → function_call to onCleanup without LHS assignment.
- **MIPC1**: `computer('arch')` call → function_call name `computer` with arg `'arch'`.

## MUST fire
```matlab
for i = 1:10
    i = 5;              % FXSET
end
import foo.bar          % SIMPT (if after other code)
x = onCleanup(@f);      % UNONC (not assigned)
c = computer('arch');   % MIPC1
fprintf('%d %d', x);    % CTPCT (2 placeholders, 1 arg)
```

## MUST NOT fire
```matlab
for i = 1:10
    y = i;
end
import foo.bar;         % SIMPT (first statement)
h = onCleanup(@f);      % UNONC assigned
c = computer;           % MIPC1 not fired (no 'arch')
fprintf('%d', x);       % CTPCT matches
```

## Files
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — add sub-check methods + dispatch, module doc rows, tests.
- `docs/rules.md` — rows. `zensical.toml` — nav entries.

## Tests
fires/not-fires per check; config disabled.

## Pitfalls
- GTARG/LTARG need arity info; if the engine has no function-signature data, implement conservatively (e.g., only for well-known functions) or defer with a note.
- SIMPT: import must be a statement at the top of the block.
- FXSET: only the loop's own iterator var.
- Confirm AST shapes with astprobe.

# GOODPRAC G5 — Structure/String/Misc (10 checks) — Plan

**Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — GoodPracticesEngine. All checks gated by `is_check_enabled`.

## Checks & messages (all Warning)
| ID | Message |
|----|---------|
| ADPROP | Use app.VAR_NAME to refer to this property. |
| ADPROPLC | Use app.VAR_NAME to reference a property of app. |
| COMFS | This comma makes the file a script. Therefore, all functions in the file are local functions. |
| DUALC | Command might be prematurely ended by comma. |
| RMFLD | RMFIELD output must be assigned back to the structure. |
| RMWRN | The warning with tag VAR_NAME has been removed from MATLAB, so this statement has no effect. |
| SEMFS | This semicolon makes the file a script. Therefore, all functions in the file are local functions. |
| SHVAU | Confusing usage of name VAR_NAME on lines VAR_NUMBER and VAR_NUMBER. Initialize VAR_NAME before line VAR_NUMBER to make it a shared variable or rename. |
| STFLD | SETFIELD output must be assigned back to the structure. |
| STRSZ | Use STRCMP to compare character vectors that can have different sizes. |

## Detection

### Node-level (function_call / field_expression / block dispatch)
- **ADPROP/ADPROPLC**: `app.PropertyName` field access (App Designer) → field_expression whose base is `app`.
- **RMFLD**: `rmfield(s, 'f')` used as statement without assignment → function_call `rmfield` whose parent is not an assignment LHS.
- **STFLD**: `setfield(s, ...)` used as statement without assignment → function_call `setfield` not assigned back.
- **RMWRN**: `warning('tag', ...)` where tag was removed from MATLAB (e.g. specific removed tags) → warning with a known-removed tag; conservative: flag warning tags matching a small denylist or all tags if uncertain (document). Best-effort.
- **STRSZ**: comparing char vectors of different sizes with `==`/`~=` → comparison_operator on strings where operands are char vectors → suggest strcmp. (Similar to existing STCMP check; STRSZ is the different-sizes variant.)
- **COMFS/SEMFS**: a comma/semicolon at the top level of a file with functions makes it a script → file-level: top-level comma/semicolon statement in a file that also contains function_definition. (Note: SEMFS already implemented? Check — the implemented list did NOT include SEMFS/COMFS.)
- **DUALC**: command might be prematurely ended by comma → command node followed by comma in a command-syntax statement.
- **SHVAU**: confusing usage of same name in different roles → symbol table analysis (name used as both function and variable, or shared-variable ambiguity). Best-effort.

## MUST fire
```matlab
s = struct('a',1);
rmfield(s, 'a');        % RMFLD (result not assigned)
app.WindowTitle = 'x';  % ADPROP
x = 'abc' == 'abcd';    % STRSZ
```

## MUST NOT fire
```matlab
s = rmfield(s, 'a');    % RMFLD assigned
app.WindowTitle;        % ADPROP read ok? (this is a read — fires ADPROPLC? verify)
x = strcmp('abc', 'abcd');
```

## Files
- `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — add sub-check methods + dispatch, module doc rows, tests.
- `docs/rules.md` — rows. `zensical.toml` — nav entries.

## Tests
fires/not-fires per check; config disabled.

## Pitfalls
- RMFLD/STFLD: only fire when the call is a standalone statement (parent is block/source_file), not when assigned.
- COMFS/SEMFS need file-level context (file contains both top-level statements and functions) — may need hybrid engine or file-level walk.
- RMWRN: conservative — flag warning tags on a known removed-tag list; document if the list is small.
- STRSZ: distinguish from the existing STCMP check (== on char vs strcmp).
- SHVAU is best-effort; document limitation.
- Confirm AST shapes with astprobe.

# GOODPRAC G1 — OOP/Class/Property Rules (13 implemented, 11 deferred, 2 excluded)

**Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices.rs` — GoodPracticesEngine. All checks gated by `is_check_enabled`, sub-checks of the hybrid engine.

## Scope summary

| Status | Count | IDs |
|--------|-------|-----|
| **Implement now** | 13 | ATTF, ATTOF, MCPO, MCSAC, MOBSRV, MDEPIN, MCCPI, MGMD, MCCPE, MTHANS, MHERM, MIPC1, MNUML |
| **Deferred** | 11 | ADPROP, ADPROPLC, MCCSPS, MCHDP, MCHDT, MCNPN, MCNPR, MCVM, MCSNOV, MCSOH, MCSUP |
| **Excluded** | 2 | M3COL (→G3/performance), CTOINW (reassigned to another group) |

### Deferred check rationale

| Check | Reason |
|-------|--------|
| ADPROP / ADPROPLC | Require `field_expression` in TARGET_NODES + "App Designer context" is undeterminable from parse tree. `app` is a common variable name outside App Designer → high false-positive rate. |
| MCCSPS | "Constant property not modified" requires scanning all assignments in class body for property writes — needs a non-trivial tree walk beyond current file-level patterns. |
| MCHDP / MCHDT | Handle-type detection requires type resolution. Text-based heuristic (default_value contains `(`) has very high false-positive rate (`zeros(3)` would trigger). |
| MCNPN / MCNPR | Need full symbol resolution within class context to distinguish property/method/event references from local variables and external functions. |
| MCVM / MCSNOV / MCSOH / MCSUP | Need deep method body analysis (control flow to detect object modification + return-value analysis). |

## Checks & messages (all Warning)

| ID | Message (from GP_messages.txt) |
|----|------|
| ATTF | The Code Analyzer is unable to determine if the expression assigned to the VAR_NAME attribute evaluates to true or false. |
| ATTOF | Setting the class attribute Abstract to false is not recommended. |
| MCPO | VAR_NAME property has no effect in a value class. |
| MCSAC | SetAccess cannot be set on Constant properties. |
| MOBSRV | Using SetObservable or GetObservable on a Constant property has no effect. |
| MDEPIN | Default values should not be assigned to dependent properties because dependent properties do not store the values. |
| MCCPI | Initialize the Constant property or make it an Abstract Constant property. |
| MGMD | 'get' method should be implemented for each dependent property that does not also have private 'GetAccess' attribute. |
| MCCPE | Attempting to call a property or event VAR_NAME as a function. |
| MTHANS | Using ANS as a method name is not recommended as ANS is frequently overwritten by MATLAB. |
| MHERM | Parenthesize the multiplication of VAR_NAME and its transpose to ensure the result is Hermitian. |
| MIPC1 | Calling the computer function with 'arch' returns 'win64', 'glnxa64', or 'maci64'. |
| MNUML | To create a square matrix, use VAR_NAME(numel(...), numel(...)). Alternatively, use VAR_NAME(size(...)) to create an array with same size as input array. |

## Existing infrastructure

The engine already implements OOP checks (CPROP, NOIN, PROP, MEXCEP, DISPLAY). The `analysis/metadata.rs` FileMeta/ClassMeta/PropertyMeta/FunctionMeta provide class structure. Engine is hybrid: `check()` for node-level, `check_file()` for file-level with `FileMeta::build()` and `SymbolTable::build()`.

Key metadata fields available:
- `ClassMeta.attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>` — class-level attributes (Abstract, Sealed, etc.)
- `ClassMeta.is_handle()` — checks if superclass list includes `handle`
- `ClassMeta.is_abstract()` — checks Abstract attribute
- `PropertiesBlockMeta.attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>` — block-level attributes (Constant, Dependent, SetObservable, etc.)
- `PropertyMeta.default_value: Option<String>` — default value text
- `PropertyMeta.has_default: bool`
- `FunctionMeta.name: String` — function/method name (includes `set.`/`get.` prefix)
- `FunctionMeta.is_method: bool`, `is_setter: bool`, `is_getter: bool`
- `AttributeMeta { name, value: Option<String>, negated: bool }`

**TARGET_NODES do not need modification** for this batch. All node-level checks use existing subscribed types (`binary_operator`, `function_call`).

## Detection (grouped by implementation layer)

### A. File-level metadata checks (add to `check_file()`)

These iterate `FileMeta.class` properties/attributes. No tree walks needed beyond `FileMeta::build()`.

#### ATTOF — Abstract = false
```
FileMeta → class.attributes → find name=="Abstract", value==Some("false"), negated==false
→ fire on the attribute's byte range
```

#### ATTF — Abstract attribute with non-literal value
```
FileMeta → class.attributes → find name=="Abstract" where value is NOT one of:
  "true", "false", "1", "0", "on", "off" (case-insensitive)
→ fire: the linter cannot determine the boolean value
```

#### MCPO — Property with no effect in value class
```
FileMeta → class is NOT handle → iterate properties_blocks
→ for each property, check block attributes for: SetObservable, GetObservable, AbortSet
→ if any of these present on a value-class property → fire
```

#### MCSAC — SetAccess on Constant properties
```
FileMeta → iterate properties_blocks
→ if block has Constant attribute (and !negated) AND any property in block (or block-level) has SetAccess → fire
→ also check per-property attributes if PropertyMeta gains attribute support; for now, block-level only
```

#### MOBSRV — SetObservable/GetObservable on Constant property
```
FileMeta → iterate properties_blocks
→ if block has Constant attribute (and !negated) AND block has SetObservable or GetObservable → fire
```

#### MDEPIN — Default value on Dependent property
```
FileMeta → iterate properties_blocks
→ if block has Dependent attribute (and !negated) → for each property with has_default==true → fire
```

#### MCCPI — Constant property without initialization, not abstract
```
FileMeta → iterate properties_blocks
→ if block has Constant attribute (and !negated) → for each property where has_default==false → fire
→ skip if class is abstract (all constants may be abstract)
```

#### MGMD — Dependent property without get method and without private GetAccess
```
FileMeta → iterate properties_blocks
→ if block has Dependent attribute (and !negated):
  → for each property in block:
    → check if a get.<PropertyName> method exists in any methods block
    → check if the property block has GetAccess = private (or methods block has private GetAccess)
    → if neither → fire
```

#### MTHANS — Method named `ans`
```
FileMeta → iterate all methods (functions where is_method==true)
→ if method.name == "ans" → fire on the method's byte range
```

#### MCCPE — Calling a property or event as a function
```
FileMeta → collect all property names from all properties_blocks
           collect all event names from all events_blocks
→ tree walk: find all function_call nodes in the class body
→ if function_call name matches a property or event name → fire
→ for field_expression calls like obj.Prop(args): extract the field name and check
```
This is a **hybrid** check: needs metadata + tree walk. Implement as file-level in `check_file()`.

### B. Node-level checks (add to `check()`)

These fire on specific tree-sitter node patterns during DFS traversal.

#### MHERM — `x*x'` without parentheses
Subscribe: `binary_operator` (already in TARGET_NODES).

```
check for binary_operator where:
  operator is `*` or `.*`
  AND one child (left or right) is a postfix_operator with `'` (ctranspose)
→ fire suggesting parenthesization

Detection within check_mherm():
  node.kind() == "binary_operator"
  text contains "*" (but not ".*" for this check, or include both)
  examine children: look for a child whose text ends with `'`
  or walk children to find postfix_operator nodes
```

Actually, the tree structure for `x*x'` is:
```
binary_operator "x*x'"
  identifier "x"
  * "*" (anon)
  postfix_operator "x'"
```

```rust
fn check_pfrni(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    if !self.is_check_enabled("PFRNI") || node.kind() != "for_statement" {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    // Confirm this is a parfor
    if !node_text(node, source).starts_with("parfor") {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    // Find the iterator → range node
    let range = find_iterator_range(node);
    let range = match range {
        Some(r) => r,
        None => return Vec::new(),
    };
    // Count named children: 2 = start:end (implicit step 1), 3 = start:step:end
    let named_count = count_named_children(range);
    if named_count != 3 {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let pos = node.start_position();
    vec![Diagnostic {
        rule_id: "PFRNI",
        message: "Do not specify the increment explicitly. The parfor loop can only use an increment of one".to_string(),
        severity: Severity::Warning,
        byte_range: range.start_byte()..range.end_byte(),
        line: pos.row + 1,
        column: pos.column + 1,
        fix: Some(Fix::new(range.start_byte()..range.end_byte(), format!(
            "{}:{}", 
            node_text(range.child(0).unwrap(), source),
            node_text(range.child(2).unwrap(), source)  // skip step, use end
        ))),
    }]
}
```

```rust
fn check_parallel_dataflow(&self, tree: &Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    let sym = SymbolTable::build(tree, source);
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    
    // Find all parfor nodes
    let parfor_nodes = collect_parfor_nodes(tree.root_node());
    
    for pf in parfor_nodes {
        let index_var = extract_parfor_index_var(pf, source);
        let pf_start = pf.start_byte();
        let pf_end = pf.end_byte();
        
        // Find the enclosing scope
        if let Some(scope) = sym.scope_at(pf_start) {
            // PFIIN: variables used in parfor body but not defined before parfor
            // PFOUS: variables assigned in parfor body but not used after parfor
            // PFTUSW: variables assigned in parfor body but used after parfor (line ref)
            // PFUIXW: index variable used after parfor (line ref)
        }
    }
    diagnostics
}
```

#### PFIIN — Input variable not initialized before parfor

For each variable **read** inside the parfor body (uses with byte_range within pf_start..pf_end), check if there is a **definition** of that variable with byte_range < pf_start. If not, fire PFIIN.

**Reliability: Moderate.** False positive possible if variable is a function input or global.

#### PFOUS — Output variable not used after parfor

For each variable **assigned** inside the parfor body (defs with byte_range within pf_start..pf_end, kind == Assignment), check if there is a **usage** of that variable with byte_range > pf_end. If not, fire PFOUS.

**Reliability: Moderate.** False positive if variable is used in a subsequent function or if the assignment is to an array element.

#### PFTUSW — Temporary variable used after parfor on line N

Same as PFOUS but when there IS a use after parfor, report the line number of that use. This is a superset: PFTUSW fires when the variable is both assigned in parfor AND used after parfor (but the value from inside the loop isn't available for temporaries).

**Actually, re-reading the MATLAB docs:** PFTUSW fires for variables that are assigned inside the parfor body but are NOT classified as sliced outputs or reductions — these are "temporary" variables whose values are NOT guaranteed to be available after the loop. The rule warns that the post-loop use may not see the expected value.

**Reliability: Moderate.** We can identify variables assigned in the parfor body. We can't perfectly distinguish temporaries from sliced outputs without reduction analysis. Conservative approach: fire PFTUSW for any variable assigned in parfor that is also used after parfor, unless it's the index variable (covered by PFUIXW).

The index variable (extracted from the `iterator` child) is used after the parfor loop ends. This is the most reliable dataflow check since we know the index variable name.

**Reliability: High.** We know the exact variable name.

```rust
fn check_compnop(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    if !self.is_check_enabled("COMPNOP") || node.kind() != "comparison_operator" {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let op = find_operator_text(node, source);
    if op != "==" { return Vec::new(); }

    let rhs = node.child(2)?;
```

```rust
fn check_compnot(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    if !self.is_check_enabled("COMPNOT") || node.kind() != "comparison_operator" {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let op = find_operator_text(node, source);
    let (expected_literal, is_negated) = match op.as_str() {
        "~=" => ("true", true),
        "==" => ("false", true),
        _ => return Vec::new(),
    };

    let lhs = node.child(0)?;
    let rhs = node.child(2)?;

    let (call_node, other_text) = if lhs.kind() == "function_call" && rhs.kind() == "identifier" {
        (lhs, node_text(rhs, source))
    } else if rhs.kind() == "function_call" && lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
        (rhs, node_text(lhs, source))
    } else { return Vec::new(); };

    if other_text != expected_literal { return Vec::new(); }

    let func_text = node_text(call_node, source);
    let replacement = format!("~{func_text}");
    let pos = node.start_position();
    vec![Diagnostic {
        rule_id: "COMPNOT",
        message: format!(
            "This logical comparison simplifies to ~{func_text}. Did you mean to use ~{func_text} to evaluate function argument: ~{func_text}(...)?"
        ),
        severity: Severity::Warning,
        byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
        line: pos.row + 1,
        column: pos.column + 1,
        fix: Some(Fix::new(node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(), replacement)),
    }]
}
```

```rust
/// Find the operator text in a binary/boolean/comparison operator node.
fn find_operator_text<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> String {
    let mut cursor = node.walk();
    for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
        if !child.is_named() {
            let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
            let trimmed = text.trim();
            if !trimmed.is_empty()
                && trimmed != "("
                && trimmed != ")"
                && trimmed != ","
            {
                return trimmed.to_string();
            }
        }
    }
    if let Some(op_node) = node.child_by_field_name("operator") {
        return node_text(op_node, source).trim().to_string();
    }
    String::new()
}
```

| TLEV | VAR_NAME could be very inefficient unless it is a top-level statement in its function. |
| UNONC | Assign the onCleanup output argument to a variable. Do not use the tilde operator (~) in place of a variable. |

- `function_call` — CTPCT, TLEV, UNONC, MIPC1
- `command` — SIMPT (import is parsed as a `command` node)
- `for_statement` — FXSET

### Check details

#### CTPCT — format/arg count mismatch

**Targets:** `function_call` nodes named `sprintf` or `fprintf`.

**Logic:**
1. Get the first argument (format string) from the `arguments` child.
2. Extract the string literal text (strip quotes).
3. Count format specifiers: scan for `%` followed by a conversion character (`d`, `f`, `s`, `e`, `g`, `x`, `o`, `c`, `u`, `i`, `p`, `t`), excluding `%%` (escaped percent).
4. Do NOT count `%*d` (width-suppressed specifiers) — the `*` means the width comes from an argument, but the conversion still consumes an arg. Actually, `%*d` consumes TWO args (width + value). For simplicity in v1, count each `%` + specifier as 1 arg. Skip `%*` patterns (they consume the width arg separately).
5. Count remaining arguments (total arg count minus the format string arg).
6. If placeholder count != arg count → fire.

**Edge cases to handle:**
- `%%` → literal percent, do not count
- `%*d` → width from arg + value from arg = 2 args (for v1: flag as potential mismatch but don't crash)
- `%n$s` → positional, does not consume sequential arg (skip these for v1)
- No format string argument → do not fire (not a format call)

#### FXSET — loop index assigned inside its own loop

**Targets:** `for_statement` nodes.

**Logic:**
1. Extract iterator variable name from the `for_statement` node.
   - Walk children: find `iterator` or `assignment` child, then find its first `identifier` child (pattern from `bugs.rs:1912`).
2. Find the `block` child (loop body).
3. Walk the block's named children. For each `assignment` node:
   - Get the `left` field name.
   - If it matches the iterator variable name → fire.
4. Only fire on direct assignments in the loop body, NOT in nested functions/lambdas inside the loop.

**Helper needed:** A recursive walk that stops at nested `function_definition` / `lambda` boundaries.

#### SIMPT — import not first statement in function

**Targets:** `command` nodes.

**Logic:**
1. Check command name is `import` (via `get_command_name`).
2. Find the parent block (walk up: parent should be `block`).
3. Find the enclosing `function_definition` (walk up further). If none → do not fire (SIMPT is function-level only).
4. Get the first named non-comment child of the block.
5. If the first named child is NOT this `import` command → fire.
6. The message includes the enclosing function name.

**Note:** `import` at the file/script level does NOT trigger SIMPT (per original MATLAB behavior).

#### TLEV — inefficient function not top-level

**Targets:** `function_call` nodes.

**Logic:**
1. Check function name is in the TLEV function list: `["eval", "evalc", "evalin", "feval"]`.
2. Check if the `function_call` is at statement level using `is_statement_level(node)`.
3. If NOT at statement level (i.e., used as a sub-expression) → fire.

**TLEV targets dynamic-code functions, not output functions like `disp`/`fprintf`.**

#### UNONC — onCleanup result not assigned

**Targets:** `function_call` nodes.

**Logic:**
1. Check function name is `onCleanup`.
2. Check parent node:
   - If parent is `assignment` → check if LHS is `~` (an `ignored_argument` node). If so → fire (tilde assignment doesn't capture the handle).

   - If parent IS `assignment` and LHS is a real variable → do NOT fire.
3. Also handle `[~] = onCleanup(...)` pattern: parent is `assignment`, LHS is a matrix containing only `~`.

#### MIPC1 — computer('arch') call

**Targets:** `function_call` nodes.

**Logic:**
1. Check function name is `computer`.
2. Check arguments: exactly one argument, which is a string literal containing `arch` (i.e., `'arch'` or `"arch"`).
3. If matched → fire.

```rust
fn check_rmfld(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    if !self.is_check_enabled("RMFLD") || node.kind() != "function_call" {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let func_name = match get_function_call_name(node, source) {
        Some(n) => n,
        None => return Vec::new(),
    };
    if func_name != "rmfield" {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    // Only fire if NOT assigned (parent is not assignment LHS)
    if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
        if parent.kind() == "assignment" {
            // Check if this function_call is the RHS (assigned), not LHS
            if let Some(lhs) = parent.child_by_field_name("left") {
                if lhs == node {
                    return Vec::new(); // This is LHS, skip
                }
            }
        }
    }
    // Also skip if at statement level (parent is source_file/block)
    // Actually, we WANT to fire when it's a standalone statement
    // The check is: fire when the call is NOT assigned back
    let pos = node.start_position();
    vec![Diagnostic {
        rule_id: "RMFLD",
        message: "RMFIELD output must be assigned back to the structure".to_string(),
        severity: Severity::Warning,
        byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
        line: pos.row + 1,
        column: pos.column + 1,
        fix: None,
    }]
}
```

```rust
fn check_comfs_semfs(&self, tree: &tree_sitter::Tree, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
    let root = tree.root_node();
    
    // Check if file contains function definitions
    let has_functions = has_child_of_kind(root, "function_definition");
    if !has_functions {
        return diagnostics;
    }
    
    // Walk top-level children for commas/semicolons
    let mut cursor = root.walk();
    for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
        if child.kind() == "," && self.is_check_enabled("COMFS") {
            let pos = child.start_position();
            diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
                rule_id: "COMFS",
                message: "This comma makes the file a script. Therefore, all functions in the file are local functions.".to_string(),
                severity: Severity::Warning,
                byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
                line: pos.row + 1,
                column: pos.column + 1,
                fix: None,
            });
        }
        if child.kind() == ";" && self.is_check_enabled("SEMFS") {
            let pos = child.start_position();
            diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
                rule_id: "SEMFS",
                message: "This semicolon makes the file a script. Therefore, all functions in the file are local functions.".to_string(),
                severity: Severity::Warning,
                byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
                line: pos.row + 1,
                column: pos.column + 1,
                fix: None,
            });
        }
    }
    diagnostics
}
```

```rust
fn check_strsz(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
    if !self.is_check_enabled("STRSZ") {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    if node.kind() != "comparison_operator" && node.kind() != "binary_operator" {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    let text = node_text(node, source);
    if !text.contains("==") && !text.contains("~=") {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    
    // Check if both operands are string literals of different lengths
    let left = node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0));
    let right = node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(1));
    
    if let (Some(l), Some(r)) = (left, right) {
        if l.kind() == "string" && r.kind() == "string" {
            let l_text = node_text(l, source);
            let r_text = node_text(r, source);
            // Compare lengths (excluding quotes)
            if l_text.len() != r_text.len() {
                let pos = node.start_position();
                return vec![Diagnostic {
                    rule_id: "STRSZ",
```

```rust
fn check_rmwrn(&self, node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
```
